newsitem.title: FRANCE: AIDS makes mark on young French people.
newsitem.headline: AIDS makes mark on young French people.

text.p: Young French people regard the spread of AIDS as the most important event in their lifetimes, ahead of the fall of the Berlin Wall, an opinion poll showed on Thursday.
A BVA survey for the daily Le Monde said 21 percent of people aged 20-35 rated the increase in the fatal AIDS disease as the event that had most marked their generation.
Fifteen percent said the 1989 fall of the Berlin Wall and collapse of the communist bloc were the most significant events, ahead of seven percent who named the 1991 Gulf War and rising unemployment.
While 85 percent said they considered themselves to be happy, nearly three out of five said they were worried about their personal and professional futures.
A total of 638 young people were interviewed from October 9 to 14 for the survey.
